newsitem.title: USA: DeKalb gets patent for corn hybrid.
newsitem.headline: DeKalb gets patent for corn hybrid.

text.p: DeKalb Genetics Corp said Tuesday that it was granted a U.S. patent for transgenic corn plants containing a bar or pat gene, giving the plant resistance to the herbicide glufosinate.
The patent is directed to the corn product itself and is not limited to any particular transformation method, DeKalb said.
Transgenic corn containing a bar or pat gene has been genetically altered to give it certain attributes, such as resistance to the use of certain herbicides.
In this case, farmers may spray their fields with glufosinates to kill weeds without harming the corn corp.
In genetic transformation, bar or pat genes are used as markers, to aid in the genetic alterration of a crop, or to confer resistance to glufosinate.

"The patent strengthens DeKalb's ability to license or exchange technology with other companies planning to market products containing either a bar or pat gene whether as a selectable marker or as a source of glufosinate resistance," Bruce Bickner, DeKalb chairman, said in a statement.
DeKalb said it began marketing test quantities of a corn hybrid resistant to glufosinate this past spring.

Both the U.S. Food and Drug Administration and the U.S. Department of Agriculture have completed their reviews of DeKalb's glufosinate-resistant corn, and the product now has all approvals required for commercial release in the United States, DeKalb said.
